text: Paya is a town and municipality located in the La Libertad Province within the Colombian department of Boyacá. It shares borders with Pisba, Labranzagrande (in Boyacá), Támara, Nunchía, and Yopal (in Casanare). The name Paya in the Chibcha language means "People of hope." Prior to the Spanish conquest in the 1530s, the area was inhabited by the Muisca, who were part of the loose Muisca Confederation. Modern Paya was officially established on September 14, 1600. The primary economic activity in Paya is horticulture, contributing 47% to the local economy, followed by livestock farming at 37% and agriculture at 16%. Its geographic coordinates are 5°38′N 72°26′W (5.633°N 72.433°W).
